title: Partner AI Customization
readerIntent: Configure AI for a customer application without modifying Nodics core.
priorKnowledge: Know the application, users, data, tools, risk, providers, and budget.
owner: Customer project modules and configuration layered over reusable AI contracts
summary: Partners customize provider profiles, prompts, corpora, tools, policies, budgets, workflows, content, and branding through explicit modules and configuration.

sections.heading: Configuration-first choices
items: Enable only required AI modules and provider adapters.
Select usage profiles and allowed models, then configure project-owned budgets and token policy without copying provider definitions into topology modules.

Reuse vendor-owned endpoint defaults, opaque secret-reference conventions, capabilities, and reviewed pricing; override only genuine customer or deployment differences through the appropriate configuration layer.
Contribute application-owned knowledge sources and classification/locale/audience policy.
Create versioned approved prompts and Assistant definitions.
Allowlist read tools and confirmation/workflow-governed mutations.
Configure retention, redaction, citations, observability, and business-facing content.

sections.heading: Application examples
items: Axis operational assistant for employee business data and actions.
Nodics documentation assistant using published documentation corpus.
Logistics assistant using that project's schemas, APIs, workflows, and guides.
Commerce support assistant using permission-safe Product, Price, Stock, order, and content contracts.
Customer support chatbot in a separate deployment and audience from an employee BackOffice assistant.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: First reuse an existing Assistant, source, tool, provider, prompt, and policy. Next override configuration in the customer project. Extend an existing adapter or service only when configuration cannot express the requirement, and implement a new authority only as the final option.

Keep credential values in governed runtime secret systems and reference them only through opaque secret references. Put vendor defaults in the vendor adapter, reusable business policy in the customer project module, and only real deployment differences in the environment module.

Keep server and node configuration limited to active modules, gateway enablement, active-provider selection, and concise profile-to-provider/model binding. Do not make a generated server or node a duplicate owner of endpoints, pricing, credentials, token policy, resilience, ledger, or business behavior.
Put application schemas and business services in their owning backend modules, and keep responsive renderers in the frontend repository.
Register contributed adapters through existing registry contracts. Do not add direct imports, parallel loaders, generic database access, or a second list of modules and tools.

Keep user-facing labels, help, errors, and localized fragments backend-content driven while frontend component renderers remain small, individually navigable, testable, and free of business decisions.

sections.heading: Deployment and extension
items: Each customer project has its own Axis/assistant deployment and effective configuration.
Tenant and project data never mix through shared conversations, corpora, ledgers, caches, or search records.
Add providers and source adapters behind provider-neutral contracts; never import vendor SDKs into callers.
Frontend owns responsive rendering and localized labels; backend owns content definitions, orchestration, security, usage, tools, and business rules.

sections.heading: Partner acceptance checklist
items: Document the purpose, audiences, data classifications, permitted corpora, operations, provider profiles, budgets, retention, regions, human escalation, and owner before enabling a deployment.
Validate positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, recovery, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, performance, cost, and regression behavior.
Prove tenant and project isolation across conversations, retrieval indexes, caches, usage ledgers, workflow carriers, logs, metrics, and provider requests.
Provide beginner setup, business operation, developer extension, provider qualification, troubleshooting, rollback, and evidence guidance alongside the implementation.
